display.name: Vercel
display.blurb: Inspect Vercel projects, deployments, build logs, domains, and teams — authenticated with a brokered Vercel access token (Bearer), injected at the egress proxy and never seen by the agent.

cli.doc:
Use `vercel` to inspect a Vercel account from this session — projects, deployments, build logs, domains, and teams via the Vercel REST API (api.vercel.com). Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects the real, capability-scoped Vercel access token (Authorization: Bearer …) on every request; `VERCEL_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder. Do NOT run any login or set a real token. This is NOT the official `vercel` deploy CLI — it is a thin REST wrapper.

Most commands accept an optional `--team <teamId>` (sent as the `?teamId=` query param) to act on a team scope instead of your personal account.

Identity check: `vercel whoami` (GET /v2/user). Needs `user:read`.
List projects: `vercel projects` (GET /v10/projects). Project env vars: `vercel env <projectIdOrName>` (GET /v10/projects/{id}/env). Both need `projects:read`. Create/update/delete a project needs `projects:write`.
List deployments: `vercel deployments [app=NAME projectId=… limit=…]` (GET /v7/deployments). One deployment: `vercel deployment <idOrUrl>` (GET /v13/deployments/{id}). Build logs: `vercel logs <idOrUrl>` (GET /v3/deployments/{id}/events). All need `deployments:read`. Triggering/cancelling a deployment needs `deployments:write`.
List domains: `vercel domains` (GET /v5/domains). Needs `domains:read`.
List teams: `vercel teams` (GET /v2/teams). Needs `teams:read`.
Any other endpoint: `vercel get <path> [key=value …]` for a GET (query params), or `vercel api <METHOD> <path> [json-body]` for any method (e.g. `vercel api POST /v13/deployments '{"name":"x"}'`). Paths are full like `/v10/projects`. A call to a path/method your profile didn't grant is denied at the network boundary, not authenticated.
